A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REFORM framework and ROM dataset. Their readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable matching despite substantial supplementary-content removal and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original REFORM benchmark results, ablations, generalization and missing-modality experiments, and human studies.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results and ablations and adds a teacher-rationale audit and a smaller-teacher experiment.

M1.justification: The cognitive priming module, dual decoders, three training stages, losses, GRPO rewards, and DGM4 token-reward adaptation are retained. The smaller teacher is an experimental control, not a revision of the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 removes evaluations on MiRAGe, AIGUARD, COSMOS, DiffFace, and DiFF, eliminating substantial coverage of non-news, e-commerce, and diffusion-based manipulation scenarios. Fine-grained MMFakeBench evaluation and missing-modality scenarios also disappear. ROM, DGM4, and binary MMFakeBench evaluation remain.

E2.justification: The reported ROM comparisons lose fine-tuned DeepSeek-VL2-3B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B from v1 Table 10. Removing the expanded MMFakeBench comparison also removes Otter-Image, MiniGPT4, VILA, and BLIP2 comparators from that benchmark. Comparator membership in retained Tables 1-3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 removes the inference-time masking protocol and the human-study designs using 117 detection samples and 193 student-explanation samples with 18 volunteers. It adds a distinct blinded audit of 350 ROM teacher rationales and a Guardian-setting control using Qwen2.5-VL-3B as teacher. Retained training settings are unchanged; these are different experimental designs, not an enlarged version of the earlier human study.

E4.justification: V2 adds teacher-rationale faithfulness and teacher-size sensitivity analyses in Section 4.3/Table 6. It removes missing-modality robustness tests, human assessment of REFORM explanations, qualitative generalization examples, and four documented failure cases. The component, token-length, consistency-margin, reward, and generation-group ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new audit and teacher comparison also report point estimates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1-5 retain their numerical results, including MMFakeBench binary test F1 of 74.1. New Table 6 reports visual/textual evidence recall of 83.7%/82.2% and smaller-teacher ACC/mAP/mIoU of 80.68/66.29/81.13. Numerous supplementary results disappear, including MMFakeBench fine-grained test F1 of 37.3, broader generalization scores, missing-modality results, and human-study outcomes. The smaller-teacher scores are newly reported conditions, not revised performance under the original teacher.

T1.justification: Equations 1-14, including semantic alignment, GRPO, and the DGM4 token reward, are retained. No substantive mathematical definition, derivation, assumption, or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about reasoning-driven detection, the three-stage REFORM framework, ROM, and superior cross-domain and zero-shot performance. The shortened title does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations that teacher rationales contain concrete evidence and that effectiveness persists with a smaller teacher, and reframes the teacher-dependence limitation. It removes substantive discussions of temporal hallucination, semantic masking of facial artifacts, low-quality imagery, and out-of-distribution perception failures, alongside interpretations of the omitted human and generalization studies.

D1.justification: V2 removes ROM source-data and construction details, domain counts, the 8:1:1 split disclosure, and fine-tuned baseline LoRA settings from v1 Appendices D-E. Core implementation settings and the four prompt templates remain in renumbered appendices. These are losses of documentation, not evidence that the underlying settings changed. The reported code URL and controlled-access policy remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lian et al. (2024) and two short-video misinformation papers, replaces the Olan citation, and removes references associated with deleted datasets, construction procedures, and comparators. The central positioning against result-oriented detection methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The supplementary narrative is substantially reorganized: most sections and the contents list disappear, while old Appendices B and G become A and B. Ethical considerations move into the main text, Section 4.3 and acknowledgments are added, and the title is shortened. Most method prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 removes v1 Figures 5-13 and Tables 6-11, including human-study displays, supplementary comparisons, dataset-construction diagrams, and qualitative cases. It adds a two-part teacher-analysis Table 6. The four prompt figures are retained and renumbered from 14-17 to 5-8; the principal main-text displays remain.

improvement.justification: The new teacher audit and smaller-teacher control strengthen support for the distillation strategy. However, unchanged broad claims lose substantial supporting evidence on non-news and missing-modality generalization, REFORM explanation quality, and concrete failure conditions. Removing ROM construction and split documentation also materially weakens reproducibility. These losses outweigh the focused new checks.
